name: Picky Assist
tagline: Omnichannel business messaging platform: WhatsApp API sending, chatbots, shared inbox and no-code automation flows.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software layer here is less exotic than it looks: a webhook listener, a keyword and rule engine, a contact table, a send queue, and a basic inbox UI. An agent can put a working single-number WhatsApp bot with canned flows in front of you in a session, because Meta's Cloud API is directly accessible and documented. What you cannot build is the part that is paperwork: business verification, template approval, message category pricing, deliverability hygiene, and the same logic repeated across Telegram, SMS, email and web chat. The DIY version is also single-agent by default, and turning it into a real shared inbox with assignment, notes and audit trails is where the weekend disappears. So: yes for a personal or one-business automation bot, no for anything that needs several humans answering at once across several channels.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a webhook server against the WhatsApp Cloud API that stores every inbound message in SQLite, matches it against YAML-defined keyword and regex flows to auto-reply, and exposes a single-user web inbox for manual replies and broadcasts to tagged contacts.
requirements: A Meta developer app with WhatsApp Cloud API access and a phone number that is not already on WhatsApp
Business verification with Meta before you can message beyond the test allowance
Approved message templates for any outbound message outside the 24 hour customer service window
A public HTTPS endpoint for webhooks, so a small VPS or a tunnel
Node 20 and a place to keep the token in .env
whatYouLose: Other channels: Telegram, SMS, email, Instagram, web chat, all of which Picky Assist normalizes into one pipeline
Multi-agent shared inbox with assignment, canned replies, notes and audit history
A no-code flow builder, meaning every logic change becomes a YAML edit and a restart
Prebuilt connectors to CRMs, Sheets, e-commerce carts and the long tail of webhook plumbing
Someone else absorbing Meta API changes, template rejections and number-quality warnings
moatNotes: The hard part of WhatsApp business messaging is not code, it is standing between you and Meta's approval and pricing machinery, then doing the same for five other channels.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the channel is rented. Anyone can call the Cloud API, but the surrounding reality of business verification, template categories, per-conversation pricing, quality ratings and periodic breaking changes is a job someone has to keep doing. Add the fact that most buyers want several staff answering the same number, plus Instagram and email in the same queue, plus a builder their non-technical operations person can edit, and the DIY bot stops being the same product. It is a good personal automation, not a support desk.
notes: The bot is a weekend; the channel access is not. Build it if you own one number and answer it yourself, buy it the moment a second human needs the same inbox.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted single-number WhatsApp automation server and inbox. Empty folder, no scaffolding tools beyond npm.

Stack, no alternatives: Node 20, TypeScript, Express, better-sqlite3, server-rendered EJS pages with plain fetch for actions. No React, no ORM, no auth provider, no cloud services beyond Meta's API.

In scope:
1. POST /webhook receiving WhatsApp Cloud API messages: verify the hub challenge on GET, verify the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC on POST, ack with 200 fast, then process asynchronously.
2. SQLite schema: contacts (wa_id, name, tags, last_seen, opted_out), messages (contact_id, direction, type, body, wamid, status, created_at), flows_log, outbox.
3. Flow engine reading flows.yaml at startup with hot reload on file change. Each flow: name, match (keyword list, regex, or "any"), conditions on contact tags, and a list of actions: reply_text, reply_template, set_tag, remove_tag, pause_bot_for_minutes, http_post to an external URL.
4. Human handoff: if a contact is paused or a human replied in the last 30 minutes, the bot stays silent.
5. Outbound sender module with a rate-limited queue, retries with backoff, and correct handling of the 24 hour customer service window: free-form text inside it, approved template only outside it. Refuse to send free-form outside the window and log why.
6. Inbox UI at / : contact list, conversation view, send free-form reply, pause/resume bot, edit tags. Single user, protected by one password in .env using a signed cookie session.
7. Broadcast page: pick a template by name, pick a tag, preview the recipient count, enqueue, skip opted-out contacts. STOP or UNSUBSCRIBE in any inbound message sets opted_out.
8. /health endpoint and a scripts/send-test.ts CLI.

Out of scope, do not build: other channels, multi-agent assignment, drag-and-drop flow builder, analytics dashboards, billing, AI replies, media transcoding beyond storing media IDs.

Secrets in .env only: WA_TOKEN, WA_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, WA_VERIFY_TOKEN, WA_APP_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD, SESSION_SECRET. Commit .env.example, never .env. No telemetry, no outbound calls except graph.facebook.com and explicit http_post actions.

Deliver: README with the exact Meta setup steps and the webhook URL to paste, a seeded flows.yaml with three example flows, npm run dev and npm start, and a short note in the README stating that Meta business verification and template approval are required before real traffic and that this software cannot shortcut either.
